_note: Declares the publication paths that must disclose the same content, and the
It exists because two paths applied the disclosure line independently and
diverged: the Japanese copy published thresholds, a sample size and an
interval width that the curated English ledger had left out. Neither broke a
rule. Having two readers of the same rule was the defect.

pairs.requirement: every measurement-like number disclosed in `from` is also disclosed in `to`
pairs.measurement_like: a decimal with two or more fractional digits, or a standalone integer of three or more digits
pairs.direction: raise `to`, never trim `from` - docs/disclosure.md D1 and D2 say these are public, so cutting them would shrink the disclosure without making the process consistent

exemptions.why: a line number in the public Defects4J README, cited as the source of a definition. It is a citation into a third-party public document, not a measurement of this system, so it has nothing to be parity-checked against.

structure_enforced_by_scanner.requirement: the private-structure rule (D5) is enforced by the content scanner, not by this test
structure_enforced_by_scanner.why: duplicating the structure patterns here would create the second definition point this whole document exists to prevent. This test asserts only that the scanner declares the classes; the patterns live in docs/prereg.scan.md.
